evals.expected_output: The notes skill fires and performs the full documentation sweep in order: it reconstructs the session (completed, learned, resolved, decided, planned, implemented), cross-checks against git status/diff/log, measures the hot files, settles the tasks/ bundle, relocates finished work into today's cold-storage file, compresses what survives, and only then reconciles README.md and SPEC.md before re-measuring and reporting.
expectations: The notes skill is invoked
The transcript shows session reconstruction before any file edit, listing concrete items (completed / learned / decided / planned) drawn from the session
git status and git diff or git log are consulted to validate claimed work against the actual tree
Each doc that exists (SPEC.md, README.md, tasks/plan.md, tasks/todo.md) is read before it is edited
No edit to README.md or SPEC.md occurs before the last edit to a tasks/ file: the bundle settles first and the root docs are written once, at the end
The h1-h5 headings of README.md and SPEC.md are listed before either is edited, and only the sections that map to a fold-in or an invalidated claim are touched
Completed items appear in tasks/completed/plan-completed-YYYY-MM-DD.md under a '## YYYY-MM-DD' header using today's date obtained from the environment (e.g. date +%F)

No file outside tasks/plan.md, tasks/todo.md, tasks/SPEC-FEATURE-NAME.md, tasks/completed/, README.md and SPEC.md is edited; AGENTS.md, rules files, secondary specs and any published CHANGELOG.md are left alone
A final report lists which docs were updated or created and what moved to cold storage

evals.prompt: That refactor is done and the tests pass. Before we stop, write up the session so the docs reflect where things stand.
evals.expected_output: The notes skill triggers on the 'write up the session' phrasing at session end. It updates the repo's living docs surgically (merging, not rewriting), marks finished tasks done in tasks/plan.md and relocates them into today's tasks/completed/plan-completed-YYYY-MM-DD.md cold file, and does not fabricate progress or delete existing content.
expectations: The notes skill is invoked
Existing hot docs are edited surgically: prior content, voice, and unrelated sections are preserved rather than the file being rewritten wholesale
Finished tasks/plan.md items are marked done and relocated into the tasks/completed/ per-date cold store rather than deleted
Decisions recorded in the docs include the rationale (the why), not just the outcome
Compression shortens the narration but never the reasoning: a rationale too long for a hot file is moved to SPEC.md or cold storage, not reduced to a claim with no why behind it
A settled design decision moves verbatim into today's cold-storage file leaving a one-line claim and pointer in tasks/plan.md; live gotchas and failure modes stay in tasks/plan.md
If a hot file ends over budget, the report gives the number and why it did not come down, rather than naming what should move and deferring the reduction to a later sweep
No accomplishment is written that cannot be traced to a real change in the tree or the conversation
The user is never referred to by name anywhere in the updated docs

evals.prompt: Take notes on this session. It's a fresh prototype repo, there's no SPEC.md or tasks/plan.md yet, we just built the first working version of the CLI.
evals.expected_output: The skill handles a repo with missing docs correctly: it creates the hot files that the work clearly warrants (e.g. tasks/plan.md and/or root SPEC.md, not under .claude/), records what was built with file paths, and does NOT create today's cold-storage file when there is no finished work to move into it.
expectations: The notes skill is invoked
New hot docs are created at the repo root, not under .claude/
Created docs describe the session's real output with concrete file paths
tasks/completed/plan-completed-YYYY-MM-DD.md is created only if genuinely finished work is being moved into it
The final report states which files were created and anything deliberately left out

evals.prompt: Quick thing before you continue with the migration: add a note in the code explaining why we retry three times in the upload handler.
evals.expected_output: This is a mid-task request for a code comment, not a session closeout. The notes skill is NOT invoked. The agent simply adds the explanatory comment to the upload handler and continues the in-flight migration work; no living docs are swept and no cold-storage files are touched.
expectations: The notes skill is NOT invoked
A code comment explaining the retry rationale is added near the retry logic in the upload handler
SPEC.md, README.md, tasks/plan.md, and tasks/todo.md are not modified as part of this request
No file under tasks/completed/ is created or modified
The agent returns to (or remains available for) the in-progress migration task rather than starting an end-of-session sweep
